name: Microsoft Entra ID
summary: Microsoft Entra ID includes MFA in its free tier, which needs an Azure subscription. Plan P1 costs $7 per user per month and P2 costs $10, both billed yearly. Risk-based Conditional Access is a P2 feature.

evidence.capability: second-factor methods such as app push or hardware keys

facts.text: Administrators enable authentication methods for all users or specific groups in the Authentication methods policy, and FIDO2 and Microsoft Authenticator are among the methods it manages.
Microsoft recommends a Conditional Access sign-in risk policy that requires MFA when sign-in risk is Medium or High.
Full access to Entra ID Protection features requires a Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra Suite license.
A registration campaign lets admins nudge targeted users to set up a passkey or Microsoft Authenticator, with a snooze period of 0 to 14 days and a limit on snoozes.
Microsoft's documentation says the legacy risk policies configured inside ID Protection retire on October 1, 2026, and recommends moving them to Conditional Access.

plans.name: Microsoft Entra ID Free
plans.notes: Requires a Microsoft Azure subscription. MFA listed as included

plans.name: Microsoft Entra ID P1
plans.notes: Adds Conditional Access and basic risk detection

plans.name: Microsoft Entra ID P2
plans.notes: Adds Entra ID Protection with risk-based Conditional Access

hiddenCosts: P1 and P2 are annual subscriptions that renew automatically.
Risk-based Conditional Access needs P2, which costs $3 more per user per month than P1.
